items.question: What is the correct response when the Pilot or Officer of the Watch gives the command 'Hard-a-starboard'?
options: Immediately turn the wheel to the maximum starboard angle and repeat the order.
Turn the wheel 15 degrees to starboard and wait for further instructions.
Steer a course towards the nearest visible landmark on the right side.
Ask for the specific course heading before moving the wheel.
items.explanation: Standard helm procedures require the rating to repeat the order and immediately move the wheel to the maximum angle allowed (usually 35 degrees) in the direction specified.

items.question: Where is the safest place for a deck rating to stand during mooring operations?
options: Outside of all marked snap-back zones and clear of bights.
Inside the snap-back zone to better monitor the winch drum.
Directly in front of the fairlead to guide the rope.
Straddling the rope to ensure it stays in the roller.
items.explanation: Snap-back zones are areas where a line may recoil with deadly force if it parts; ratings must always stand in designated safe areas.

items.question: Which document must be signed and posted at the entrance before any rating enters a fuel tank or chain locker?
options: Enclosed Space Entry Permit
Hot Work Permit
Bridge Logbook Entry
Bunker Delivery Note
items.explanation: An Enclosed Space Entry Permit ensures the atmosphere has been tested and safety measures are in place before entry.

items.question: What is the primary purpose of a 'Permit to Work' system on board?
options: To ensure a formal safety check is completed and risks are managed.
To record the hours worked by the crew for overtime pay.
To notify the port authorities of maintenance activities.
To allow ratings to work without supervision.
items.explanation: The Permit to Work (PTW) system is a safety management tool designed to identify hazards and ensure specific precautions are taken.

items.question: While on lookout duty at night, you see a single white light ahead. What should you report to the OOW?
options: Reporting 'Light right ahead, sir'.
Reporting 'Fishing vessel on the port bow'.
Doing nothing until you see a red or green light.
Changing the ship's course immediately.
items.explanation: A rating's duty is to report the sighting and the bearing of any light or object to the OOW immediately.

items.question: If you notice oil leaking from a hydraulic pipe during a cargo operation, what is your first action?
options: Stop the operation and notify the Officer on Duty immediately.
Find a bucket to catch the oil and continue working.
Wipe it up with a rag and tell no one.
Throw sawdust on it and wait for the end of the shift.
items.explanation: Immediate reporting and cessation of the source are critical to prevent environmental pollution and slips/falls.

items.question: What does a 'Short Blast' on the ship's whistle signify in accordance with COLREGs?
options: A duration of about one second.
A duration of four to six seconds.
A warning that the ship is sinking.
A signal to indicate the ship is at anchor.
items.explanation: Rule 32 defines a short blast as a blast of about one second's duration.

items.question: When securing a cargo container with lashing rods and turnbuckles, how should the turnbuckles be tightened?
options: Tightened until firm, but not over-stressed, and secured with locking nuts/wires.
Left loose to allow for the ship's movement and vibration.
Tightened using a long pipe for extra leverage until they cannot move.
Only hand-tightened without the use of a spanner.
items.explanation: Lashing must be firm and secured against loosening, but over-tightening can lead to rod failure under stress.

items.question: A lifebuoy equipped with a light and smoke signal is primarily used for which emergency?
options: Man Overboard (MOB).
Total Abandon Ship.
Fire in the galley.
Enclosed space rescue.
items.explanation: The light and smoke lifebuoys are positioned on the bridge wings to be released immediately during a Man Overboard event to mark the position.

items.question: According to COLREG Rule 5, what is the primary duty of a lookout on the bridge?
options: To maintain a continuous watch by sight and hearing to assess risk of collision
To clean the bridge windows and keep the coffee ready for the officer
To monitor the radar only and report targets over 5 miles away
To assist the helmsman with steering during heavy weather
items.explanation: Rule 5 requires every vessel to maintain a proper look-out at all times by sight and hearing as well as by all available means appropriate in the prevailing circumstances.

items.question: When handling synthetic fiber mooring lines, what is the safest way to stand relative to a line under tension?
options: Away from the 'snap-back' zone and never in a bight
Directly in line with the fairlead to watch the rope
Straddling the line to keep it centered
Inside the bight of the rope for better leverage
items.explanation: Standing in a snap-back zone or inside a bight is extremely dangerous as the line can snap or tighten suddenly, causing fatal injuries.

items.question: You are assigned to chip rust on deck using a pneumatic needle gun. Which set of PPE is mandatory for this specific task?
options: Safety goggles, ear protection, gloves, and safety shoes
Hard hat and safety shoes only
Lifejacket and safety harness
Latex gloves and a dust mask only
items.explanation: Pneumatic tools create flying debris (requiring eye protection) and high noise levels (requiring ear protection).

items.question: Which of the following items is permitted to be thrown overboard while the vessel is 15 nautical miles from the nearest land?
options: Food waste that has been comminuted or ground
Plastic water bottles and wrapping
Used engine oil and oily rags
Metal paint cans and empty drums
items.explanation: MARPOL Annex V prohibits the discharge of almost all garbage into the sea, with food waste being one of the few exceptions if specific distance requirements are met.

items.question: While securing cargo containers on deck, you notice a turnbuckle is bent and the threads are stripped. What should you do?
options: Report the damaged gear to the Bosun and replace it with a certified spare
Apply grease to the threads and force it to tighten with a pipe wrench
Leave it as it is, since the other lashings will hold the weight
Tie the lashings together with rope to reinforce the bent turnbuckle
items.explanation: Damaged lashing equipment must never be used as it compromises the safety of the cargo and the vessel.

items.question: What is the correct procedure for painting a surface that was recently chipped?
options: Remove dust/grease, apply primer, then apply the finish coats
Apply the finish coat directly over the bare metal to save time
Mix all paint types together before applying for a thicker layer
Paint over any remaining loose rust to seal it from the air
items.explanation: Proper surface preparation and the use of primer are essential for corrosion protection and paint adhesion.

items.question: Before entering a ballast tank, who must sign the Enclosed Space Entry Permit?
options: The Master or a designated Responsible Officer
The Deck Boy assigned to the watch
The Cook or Chief Steward
Any crew member who has been on the ship for one month
items.explanation: Formal authorization by a senior officer is mandatory to ensure all safety checks have been verified.

items.question: You are ordered to grease the mooring winch. The winch is currently running. What is the safest action?
options: Request the operator to stop and lock out the winch before greasing moving parts
Carefully apply grease to the moving gears while the winch is rotating
Throw grease at the gears from a safe distance of two meters
Wait until the winch gets hot so the grease spreads faster
items.explanation: Maintenance on moving machinery is prohibited due to the high risk of entanglement.

items.question: As an AB at the wheel, you receive the command 'Steady as she goes'. What is your immediate action?
options: Note the current compass heading and maintain the vessel on that course
Keep turning the wheel in the direction the ship was already moving
Immediately bring the rudder to midships and stop the engines
Increase the speed of the vessel to stabilize the steering
items.explanation: The command 'Steady as she goes' requires the helmsman to steer the heading noted at the moment the command was given.

items.question: What is the primary danger when standing in the 'bight' of a mooring rope?
options: Being caught and dragged if the rope suddenly tensions
The rope becoming dirty from the deck
Causing the winch to overload
Reducing the breaking strength of the rope
items.explanation: A bight is a loop; if the rope tensions suddenly, the loop closes or moves rapidly, potentially trapping or crushing a crew member.

items.question: Before entering an enclosed space, what is the minimum required oxygen content by volume?
items.explanation: The atmosphere must be tested to ensure it contains 21% oxygen by volume, which is the normal level in clean air.

items.question: A Permit to Work (PTW) for 'Hot Work' is generally valid for which duration?
options: Only for the specific period or shift stated on the permit
Until the end of the voyage
24 hours regardless of the task completion
One week
items.explanation: Permits are specific to a task and time frame; if the work is interrupted or the shift ends, the permit must be re-validated.

items.question: When chipping rust with a pneumatic needle gun, which combination of PPE is most essential?
options: Safety goggles, ear protection, and safety gloves
Safety harness and lifejacket
Rubber boots and apron
Dust mask and welding shield
items.explanation: Mechanical descaling creates high noise levels and flying debris, requiring eye and hearing protection.

items.question: You are told to lash a timber deck cargo. Which equipment is most appropriate to ensure the lashings remain tight during the voyage?
options: Turnbuckles or Load binders
Polypropylene rope hitches
Nylon cable ties
Duct tape and twine
items.explanation: Timber cargo settles; turnbuckles or load binders allow for periodic tightening during the voyage as required by the CSS Code.

items.question: Under MARPOL Annex V, where is it permitted to discharge plastic waste overboard?
options: Nowhere, it is strictly prohibited to discharge plastic anywhere at sea
Outside 12 nautical miles from land
Outside 25 nautical miles from land
Only if ground to less than 25mm
items.explanation: MARPOL Annex V prohibits the discharge of all plastics, including synthetic ropes and plastic garbage bags, into the sea.

items.question: What is the primary purpose of a 'Bulwark Ladder'?
options: To provide safe passage from the top of the bulwark to the deck
To allow the crew to paint the ship's side
To secure the pilot ladder to the ship's side
To store mooring ropes off the deck
items.explanation: Bulwark ladders are used where the pilot ladder requires the user to climb over the bulwark, ensuring safe access to the deck.

items.question: You are assigned to supervise a new Deck Boy painting in a confined area. You notice he looks dizzy. What is your priority action?
options: Immediately remove him to fresh air and stop the work
Tell him to take a 5-minute break and then finish the job
Give him a glass of water and tell him to wear a dust mask
Open a nearby door and tell him to work faster to finish
items.explanation: Dizziness is a sign of VOC inhalation or oxygen deficiency; safety of life takes precedence over task completion.
items.regulation: STCW Table A-II/5 (Contribute to safe operation)

items.question: A seaman is instructed to enter a chain locker to stow the anchor cable. Which document must be completed and displayed at the entrance before entry?
options: Enclosed Space Entry Permit
Hot Work Permit
Working at Height Permit
Cold Work Permit
items.explanation: Chain lockers are identified as enclosed spaces due to limited ventilation and the risk of oxygen depletion from rusting steel.

items.question: During mooring operations, what is the safest position for a rating to stand while a rope is under heavy tension?
options: Well away from the 'snap-back' zone
Directly behind the winch operator
Inside the bight of the rope
Next to the fairlead to monitor the chafe
items.explanation: Ratings must remain clear of snap-back zones, which are areas where a rope might recoil with fatal force if it parts.
items.regulation: COSWP Code of Safe Working Practices 26.3.2

items.question: During a 'Man Overboard' drill, what is the primary role of the designated lookout?
options: Keep the person in the water in sight at all times and point
Immediately jump in to rescue the person
Go to the bridge to take the helm
Prepare the rescue boat engine
items.explanation: Maintaining visual contact is critical because once a person is lost to sight in the sea, they are extremely difficult to relocate.

items.question: When using a pneumatic needle gun for descaling, what safety check is most important regarding the air hose?
options: Ensure a safety 'whip check' wire is installed at the coupling
Ensure the hose is painted the same color as the deck
Ensure the hose is at least 50 meters long
Ensure the hose is made of clear plastic
items.explanation: Whip checks prevent the hose from thrashing violently and causing injury if the compressed air coupling fails.

items.question: Which item must be checked on a Lifebuoy during a routine monthly inspection?
options: Retro-reflective tape and correct vessel markings
The expiration date of the internal battery
The pressure of the inflation cylinder
The weight of the buoyant smoke signal
items.explanation: Lifebuoys must have the ship's name and port of registry in Roman block letters and be fitted with retro-reflective material.

items.question: If you witness a small oil spill on deck during a bunkering operation, what is your first immediate action?
options: Shout 'Stop Pumping' and alert the person in charge
Run to the SOPEP locker to get sawdust
Try to wash the oil overboard with a fire hose
Record the incident in the Oil Record Book
items.explanation: The priority in any spill is to stop the source of the leak immediately to prevent escalation and environmental damage.

items.situation: You are the Bosun supervising a mooring operation. During the heaving of the forward spring line, you notice a strand of the synthetic rope beginning to fray and 'milk' under extreme tension.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Signal the winch operator to stop heaving immediately
Order all personnel to clear the 'snap-back' zones
Inform the Pilot and Master on the bridge of the line's condition
Slacken the line carefully to relieve tension
Replace the damaged line with a spare before continuing operations
items.critical_step: Signal the winch operator to stop heaving immediately
items.regulation: COSWP (Code of Safe Working Practices) Chapter 26

items.question: During a mooring operation, you notice a member of your team standing in a bight of a line but the Bosun has not seen it. What is your immediate course of action and why?
key_steps: Shout a clear 'Stop' command or warning immediately to the team member
Physically or verbally direct them out of the danger zone before the line takes tension
Inform the Officer on the bridge or the Bosun of the safety intervention
items.critical_step: Immediately call out the hazard to the crew member before the line comes under strain.

items.question: As an Able Seaman (AB), you are supervising an Ordinary Seaman (OS) during tank cleaning. They are not wearing their safety harness correctly. How do you lead this situation?
key_steps: Instruct the OS to stop work and explain the specific risk of the incorrectly worn harness
Demonstrate the correct method of securing the PPE as per manufacturer guidelines
Verify the OS understands the safety requirement before allowing work to resume
items.critical_step: Correcting the unsafe behavior immediately through demonstration and supervision.
items.regulation: ISM Code Part 7 (Development of Plans for Shipboard Operations)

items.question: You are part of a team painting in a confined space. A team member complains of feeling lightheaded. What is the team response protocol?
key_steps: Evacuate all personnel from the space immediately
Raise the alarm and notify the OOW/Duty Officer of a potential atmospheric hazard
Ensure no one re-enters the space without a self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA)
items.critical_step: Prohibiting re-entry into the space until it has been tested and declared safe by a competent officer.
items.regulation: IMO Resolution A.1050(27) (Revised recommendations for entering enclosed spaces)

items.situation: You are an Able Seaman (AB) acting as the lookout on the bridge during a night watch. You observe a single white light approximately 2 points on the starboard bow, but the radar does not show a target in that position. The Officer of the Watch appears to be busy with paperwork.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Continue to monitor the light using binoculars to determine its nature
Immediately inform the Officer of the Watch (OOW) of the visual sighting
Provide the relative bearing and approximate distance of the light to the OOW
Monitor for any change in the light's bearing to assess collision risk
Maintain a continuous watch until the OOW acknowledges and assesses the target
items.critical_step: Immediately inform the Officer of the Watch (OOW) of the visual sighting

items.situation: As a Bosun, you are supervising a team during mooring operations at a busy terminal. You notice that a spring line is under extreme tension and has begun to make a 'pinging' sound, while a crew member is standing directly in the snap-back zone of that line.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Order the crew member to move out of the snap-back zone immediately
Signal the winch operator to slacken the line or stop heaving
Assess the condition of the line for damage or fraying
Communicate the situation to the Pilot or Bridge team
Redeploy the line or adjust mooring configuration if necessary
items.critical_step: Order the crew member to move out of the snap-back zone immediately
items.regulation: Code of Safe Working Practices (COSWP) Chapter 26; MLC 2006 Regulation 4.3

items.situation: You are an AB performing a routine round of the vessel. In a storage locker, you notice a thick cloud of smoke coming from behind a stack of spare mooring ropes, but no flames are visible yet. There is a fire alarm call point (break-glass) 10 meters away.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Activate the nearest fire alarm call point immediately
Report the exact location and nature of the smoke to the bridge via radio
Close the door to the locker to restrict oxygen and contain the smoke
Ensure all other crew members are clear of the immediate area
Proceed to your designated muster station as per the muster list
items.critical_step: Activate the nearest fire alarm call point immediately
items.regulation: SOLAS Chapter II-2; ISM Code Section 8

items.situation: As an OS, you are instructed to enter a chain locker to assist the Bosun in clearing a twist in the anchor chain. The locker has been closed for several months and has no mechanical ventilation.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Refuse entry until an Enclosed Space Entry Permit has been issued
Verify that the atmosphere has been tested for oxygen and toxic gases
Ensure the space has been thoroughly ventilated before entry
Confirm a standby person is posted at the entrance with communication gear
Check that rescue equipment is available at the entrance
items.critical_step: Refuse entry until an Enclosed Space Entry Permit has been issued
items.regulation: IMO Resolution A.1050(27); STCW Table A-VI/1-4

items.situation: You are a Bosun supervising the lowering of a lifeboat during a drill. As the boat reaches the embarkation deck, you notice one of the falls (wire ropes) has several broken strands and appears heavily corroded near the terminal fitting.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Order the operation to stop immediately and secure the boat
Instruct all crew to step out of the lifeboat if they have boarded
Report the defect to the Chief Officer or Safety Officer
Ensure the equipment is tagged 'Out of Service' to prevent accidental use
Assist in the detailed inspection and replacement of the fall wire
items.critical_step: Order the operation to stop immediately and secure the boat
items.regulation: SOLAS Chapter III, Regulation 20; ISM Code Section 10

items.situation: While working on deck, an Ordinary Seaman (OS) notices oil leaking from a hydraulic pipe on the provision crane and dripping toward the overboard scupper. The Bosun is currently in the paint locker and cannot see the leak. No oil has reached the water yet.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Stop the crane operation immediately
Plug the scupper and contain the spill on deck with sawdust or pads
Report the leak to the Officer of the Watch (OOW) and the Bosun
Identify and mark the source of the leak for the engineers
Assist in the cleanup of the contained oil
items.critical_step: Plug the scupper and contain the spill on deck to prevent overboard discharge.
items.regulation: MARPOL Annex I - Prevention of Pollution by Oil

items.situation: A Deck Boy is cleaning the alleyway when he hears the General Emergency Alarm (seven short and one long blast). He is near his cabin but his assigned muster station is on the Boat Deck.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Stop all cleaning work immediately
Retrieve his lifejacket, immersion suit, and warm clothing from his cabin if safe
Proceed directly to his designated muster station
Report his presence to the Mustering Officer
Await further instructions from the bridge
items.critical_step: Proceed directly to his designated muster station.
items.regulation: SOLAS Chapter III, Regulation 37 (Muster list and emergency instructions)

items.situation: The Bosun is supervising a team of two ratings entering a ballast tank for inspection. The gas meter used for the initial check has just timed out, but the crew argues that the tank was vented all morning and feels 'fresh' enough to enter for a quick look.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Prohibit entry until a new atmosphere test is conducted
Verify that the Enclosed Space Entry permit is fully signed and valid
Ensure the ventilation is continuous during the entry
Check that rescue equipment is staged at the entrance
Assign a dedicated standby person at the entrance
items.critical_step: Prohibit entry until a new atmosphere test is conducted.
items.regulation: IMO Resolution A.1050(27) - Revised Recommendations for entering enclosed spaces aboard ships

items.situation: During mooring operations, an AB notices that one of the forward breast lines has become snagged on a bulbous bow of a nearby tug and is under extreme tension. The line is making a high-pitched 'singing' sound, indicating imminent failure.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Shout a warning to all crew members to clear the snap-back zones
Signal the winch operator to slacken the line immediately
Inform the Pilot or Officer in charge of the mooring station
Wait for tension to be safely released before attempting to clear the snag
Inspect the line for damage once it is slack
items.critical_step: Shout a warning to all crew members to clear the snap-back zones.
items.regulation: COSWP (Code of Safe Working Practices) Chapter 26 (Mooring Operations)

items.situation: A rating is assigned to paint the mast using a man-basket and the provision crane. Before starting, he notices that the safety latch on the crane hook is missing, but the Bosun says it is a 'short job' and he should just be careful.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Refuse to start the job using defective equipment
Report the missing safety latch to the Chief Officer
Lock out/Tag out the crane to prevent accidental use
Request a replacement hook or a certified repair
Verify all PPE (harness and fall arrestor) is in good condition
items.critical_step: Refuse to start the job using defective equipment.
items.regulation: ILO Code of Practice: Safety and health in ports/ships (Lifting Appliances)

items.situation: While the ship is at the pier, an OS sees a person from the shore attempting to board the ship via the gangway without a visitor's badge. The visitor claims they are the 'Captain's friend' and refuses to show ID to the gangway watch.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Physically block access to the deck (stay at the gangway head)
Request the individual to wait at the bottom of the gangway
Contact the Ship Security Officer (SSO) or OOW via radio
Check the visitor list provided by the agent
Maintain the security log entry regarding the encounter
items.critical_step: Contact the Ship Security Officer (SSO) or OOW via radio.
items.regulation: ISPS Code Part A, Section 7 (Access to the ship)

items.situation: During a heavy rainstorm at sea, an AB notices that the securing dogs on a weathertight hatch leading to the stores are loose, and water is starting to seep into the compartment. The ship is rolling moderately.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Notify the Bridge/OOW of the water ingress
Don appropriate PPE for working on deck in foul weather
Secure the hatch dogs tightly, following safe manual handling practices
Check the integrity of the rubber packing on the hatch
Report the completion of the task and the status of the compartment to the OOW
items.critical_step: Notify the Bridge/OOW of the water ingress.
items.regulation: International Convention on Load Lines, Regulation 16 (Hatchways)
